body:
It seems that compilation is failing because some structs are used in CowData before being defined, and MSVC cannot handle this.

I think we can make it work by reordering declarations and definitions such that `Vector<X>` is never used before `X` is defined. 
Or we switch to use compiler-defined alignment by using fake structs instead of defining alignments manually. 

I'm open to both. Before I'm implementing anything new, I'd like to hear feedback though.

Both your solutions are not doable without some massive rewrite. I guess they wanted the flexibility to be able to define `CowData<T>` without having T defined yet, and you are breaking that here. Seems like lot of trouble for a very small gain. 
I am curious though on how GCC and clang are compiling at this point, as they do not seem to in [godbolt](https://godbolt.org/z/vEd7rT1n4)

Your godbolt example did not compile because it was using `X` in a function without any definition for it at all. You can see the equivalent example compiles equivalently on GodBolt:

- https://godbolt.org/z/van944jKc (clang, success)
- https://godbolt.org/z/f4hbEEnc3 (msvc, failure)

> I guess they wanted the flexibility to be able to define CowData<T> without having T defined yet

I'm not sure that is the case, but it's hard to know without asking the original author of this section of code, because it has not been commented. My guess was that this code was simply copied over from `memory.h` without looking at it in-depth. 

> Seems like lot of trouble for a very small gain

I guess that's true; i was hoping it would just compile everywhere, because then it would not have been any trouble at all. As is so often the case, much code was built around the code in its current state with its current setup implicitly assumed, making a change difficult.

Both my solutions should work though with little effort; the second (using structs and letting the compiler align) may work out of the box, while the first should just require moving definitions above `CowData` use.
Edit: Hrm, apparently the `GDScriptDataType` problem isn't as easily resolved, since it requires its own definition to know alignment (in MSVC anyway). That makes the struct solution the only viable option.

Ok, I did some actual tests with a struct-based allocator.

Starting the launcher from b7c81d52bb988a218e19a3a199f5f2d11e4ff1a6 (struct-based) vs 25a0c9f5e750fe7c886c204dbe2b7f09cdb0b89e (current master), I'm logging allocated RAM and boot times.

Boot times are about 0.64s +- 0.03s, negligible differences in both.
Allocation size is reproducibly 316149575b in b7c81d52bb988a218e19a3a199f5f2d11e4ff1a6 (struct-based), and 314894086 in 25a0c9f5e750fe7c886c204dbe2b7f09cdb0b89e (current master). The compiler seems to want to add padding somewhere else; I'm not sure why.

In either case, it's not really worth risking a refactor for, or spending much more time on it. Therefore, I'm closing this PR in light of evidence.
